title: Opportunity Slicing: Multi-Objective LCR (Latency-Cost-ROI) Scoring for Inference Prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We propose a Multi-Objective LCR (Latency-Cost-ROI) scoring framework to rank roadmap initiatives that trade off latency improvements, unit-cost reductions, and top-line ROI. The goal is a reproducible, data-driven prioritization signal that complements RICE by making latency and cost first-class citizens and allowing PMs and eng leads to run sensitivity analyses across weighting scenarios.

Why: Current prioritization leaning heavily on subjective RICE subscores. With inference economics being central to Redwood's value prop, we need a repeatable rubric to prioritize features, runtime optimizations, and infra investments based on their combined impact on user experience (latency), unit economics (cost), and business return (ROI).

Core formula & normalization: We score each initiative on three normalized axes: ROI, Latency Benefit, Cost Benefit. Each axis is normalized to [0,1] using min-max across a candidate set (with outlier clamping at 1st/99th percentiles).

- ROI_raw: expected incremental monthly ARR in USD. ROI_norm = (ROI_raw - ROI_min)/(ROI_max - ROI_min)
- Latency_raw: expected median p50 latency delta (ms) for impacted requests (positive means improvement). Latency_norm = clamp((Latency_raw - Latency_min)/(Latency_max - Latency_min), 0, 1)
- Cost_raw: expected % unit cost reduction (positive is benefit). Cost_norm = clamp((Cost_raw - Cost_min)/(Cost_max - Cost_min), 0, 1)

Composite LCR score = w_roi * ROI_norm + w_latency * Latency_norm + w_cost * Cost_norm

Default weights (initial proposal): w_roi=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_cost=0.2. We will maintain preset weight profiles for different audiences: "Business-led" (0.65/0.2/0.15), "Platform-first" (0.35/0.35/0.3), and "Balanced" (0.5/0.3/0.2).

Tie-breakers & elasticity: For initiatives with similar LCR score we apply secondary tie-breakers: risk (engineering estimate), dependencies, and strategic alignment OKR fit. We also compute an elasticity sensitivity matrix by sweeping weights to show how rank changes under weight perturbations.

Implementation plan:
1) Define canonical input fields for each initiative: ROI_raw (USD/mo), Latency_raw (ms), Cost_raw (% unit reduction), confidence (low/med/high), affected traffic %. Add to initiative intake template.
2) Build a lightweight scoring spreadsheet and automated script in analytics to normalize historical initiatives, compute scores, and plot sensitivity bands.
3) Run backtest using last 18 months of initiatives and outcomes (link to analysis).
4) Pilot for Q2 roadmap prioritization: score ~12 candidate initiatives with Eng and GTM, iterate weight profiles.
5) Bake into roadmap review cadence (monthly scoring refresh ahead of cycle planning).

Tradeoffs & open questions:
- Normalizing ROI (USD) vs. relative business impact for early-stage/new products. Proposal: allow manual override with documented rationale.
- Latency impact estimation precision depends on instrumentation; we need ENG support to produce representative p50/p95 deltas.
- Cost estimates can be modelled using Redwood Optimize outputs but may have uncertainty; we will include confidence buckets and apply a dampening factor for low-confidence inputs.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.

Related artifacts: initial analysis deck, scoring spreadsheet, backtest notebook (analytics), proposed intake template, PRD draft for scoring UI in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical intake template added to PRD and used for pilot initiatives
Automated scoring script available in analytics repo and reviewed by Eng/Analytics
Backtest documented showing how historical priorities would have shifted (at least 10 initiatives)
Pilot of 8-12 initiatives completed and feedback captured from Eng, GTM, and Platform leads
Dashboard showing LCR score, component norms, and weight sensitivity available in Console (read-only for PMs)
